title: State of UP v. Bawariya Nomad Highway Robbery Syndicate (Bulandshahr Gang Rape)
crime_type: Armed Highway Ambush / Axle-Rod Trap / Group Dacoity & Aggravated Assault
court_or_authority: Special POCSO & Sessions Court, Bulandshahr / High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
legal_citation: Sessions Trial No. 512/2016; 2019 SCC OnLine All 4120
source: Allahabad High Court Judgment & Indian Kanoon
ipc_sections: Section 397 IPC (Robbery or dacoity, with attempt to cause death or grievous hurt)
location: Dostpur, NH-91, Bulandshahr, Uttar Pradesh, India
evidence: Recovery of heavy curved iron axle thrown across highway lanes to rupture vehicle oil pans and tires
Recovered gold jewelry and mobile phones belonging to traveling family recovered from forest camps in Mawana
Positive Test Identification Parade (TIP) by victim survivors identifying suspects under judicial magistrate supervision
DNA semen profiling matching seized biological evidence from agricultural sugarcane fields
modus_operandi: Lurked alongside unlit national highways during midnight hours. Threw heavy metal axles or stones at passing family cars to disable tires or undercarriage. Once the disabled vehicle halted, armed gang dragged occupants into nearby sugarcane fields, tied up male members, looted all jewelry and cash, and sexually assaulted female victims.
personality_disorder: Antisocial predatory nomadism, thrill dacoity, and uninhibited group sexual sadism.
common_traits: Deliberate vehicle mechanical disabling on unlit national highways
Dragging victims into tall agricultural crops (sugarcane / mustard)
Simultaneous armed dacoity and group sexual violence
Nomadic interstate flight across border district hideouts
summary: Landmark highway dacoity trial resulting in life sentences for the nomadic Bawariya gang members. Led to widespread deployment of highway patrol cruisers, automated SOS booths, and mandatory GPS tracking on national highways across North India.
